summary:
Abuja Federal Capital Territory stands under Nigeria's national framework, and no territorial variation from it was identified in this inventory: the Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014 and the criminal provisions it reinforces apply in the capital as they do elsewhere, and the national layer is carried by the parent record.

The territory's documented trans-specific killing is that of a 33-year-old transgender TikToker known as Abuja Area Mama. BBC News reported on 9 August 2024 that her beaten and bruised body was found along the Katampe-Mabushi expressway in the Banex/Wuse II area of Abuja on Thursday 8 August 2024, hours after she posted a final video; she had previously expressed fear for her life.

The police account of the death misgendered her. The Abuja police statement described the victim as "a man fully dressed in female clothing with no means of identification", and the territorial police chief, Benneth Igweh, ordered a "thorough and discreet" investigation.

No prosecution followed. The Dial (Issue 25) records that six months after the killing no suspects had been charged despite that order, and that a petition of nearly 6,000 signatures demanded investigation of her murder as a hate crime.

The most recent documented instance of trans-specific violence in this record is the August 2024 killing; no later instance is documented for the territory.
tangentialFactors:
No comparative or per-capita figure for the Federal Capital Territory is sourced: the inventory contains one documented trans-specific incident for the territory and no denominator against which its frequency could be assessed.

BBC News placed the killing against a documented national pattern, noting that although Nigerian laws guarantee freedom from discrimination, mass arrests and detention of LGBTQ+ people are common, especially in northern states. That pattern is national in scope and is carried by the parent record.
localsOnly:
Residents seeking accountability have used petition mechanisms: nearly 6,000 people signed a demand that the Area Mama killing be investigated as a hate crime, filed while the promised investigation had produced no charge.

How a victim is recorded shapes the case that follows. The official police description of the deceased as "a man fully dressed in female clothing" is the framing on which the territorial police's own file was opened, and no suspect had been charged against it six months later.
outOfScopeNotes:
The UK foreign office warning to LGBT+ travellers to Nigeria, reported on 19 August 2026, is a national advisory with no Abuja-specific breakdown in this inventory; it is carried at the national layer.

Document and marker rules, entry and screening practice, facilities access, care availability and partner recognition for the Federal Capital Territory are not sourced here. Whether any Abuja-specific enforcement pattern exists beyond the single documented killing is unresolved in this record.
